title: Koji Chicken
text:
If you’re craving top-notch fried chicken and a refreshing bubble tea in Hell’s Kitchen, Koji is a standout. The neighborhood is packed with great restaurants, but nothing else hits the same way.

I keep coming back for their Seoul Chicken Sandwich, the chicken is always crisp on the outside, juicy inside, and perfectly seasoned with just the right amount of heat and tang. The bun stays soft and fresh, and the house-made sauces pull everything together.

Their bubble tea is equally impressive bro… Balanced sweetness, chewy pearls, and a variety of flavors that complement the savory food. Service is quick and friendly, making it easy to pop in whether you’re on a lunch break or out for a late-night bite.

Whenever I’m in the area, Koji is an automatic stop. Consistently excellent food, lively vibe, and unbeatable flavors make it my go-to spot in Hell’s Kitchen.

title: Koji Chicken
text:
One of my new favorite spots for a chicken sandwich. I've only tried only two of the eight different sandwiches, but am definitely going to keep coming to try them all, as they're freshly made!

Original crispy chicken sandwich (5/5) - Undoubtedly lives up to the restaurant name - krispy outside, juicy inside! This is one heck of a chicken sandwich, as you get a generous amount of meat, and the sauce just goes really well with the burger.

Soy garlic chicken sandwich (3.5/5) - The soy garlic chicken is really well made. The first bite was amazing, but after eating about 2/3 of the burger, the sweetness is a lil overwhelming. I recommended it to my coworker who loved it over the original crispy so I guess it's just preference.

The only con is that it can take some time for the order as it's freshly made, but it's well worth the wait!

text:
came to Rokstar via a promotional event…

Rokstar Chicken Harlem is located on the second floor of the huge Food Bazaar Supermarket. serving up a fast casual menu of comfort foods like Korean fried chicken, wings, boneless fried chicken, chicken sandwiches and more plus a nice variety of side dishes. landed on a 5 Wings Combo Meal which is a main dish, one side item, a scoop of coleslaw, and a soft drink. the wings ( a mix of drums and flats) to be tossed in a Korean Sweet Chilli  sauce (there’s a variety of sauces & you can have the sauce on the side). chose the Cajun Garlic Fries as my side and a grape soda as my drink. food is made to order so it takes about 10ish minutes for a combo meal to be ready and it's well worth the wait. the wings are crispy and fairly meaty--the sweet chili sauce isn't too sweet or too hot...well balanced. the wing quality from taste to quality was really good. the fries are thin cut (sorta like shoestring style)--crispy and well-seasoned. the coleslaw was a pleasant surprise as i normally don't think about it too much as a side item but it was not too coleslaw-y nor overly sweet...a crunchy salad palate refresh of sorts to pair with the rich comfort food flavors .

the service person was very friendly and professional. i asked for recommendations and i was met with a bunch of suggestions in terms of menu tips. food was packed neatly to go with a sheet of promotional coupons for future visits. also if you want to dine at the location, there are a couple of tables set to the side.

text:
Quaint eatery!

For example, in comparison to Garlic to the Chicken, the bites of the wings and legs here didn't leave your palate with meat but rather more fried skin and oil.

However its still good. The atmosphere is okay with plenty of seating and good pop music. I think it's K-pop. The staff were cordial. They bring you your food if you're eating in and utensils which I thought was a nice hospitable touch.

The truffle fries were average. They need to add more garlic and truffle sauce rather than oregano, parmesan flakes and some salt.

The portions are decent so come hungry lest you risk taking food home.

Overall I'd say a decent Korean Fried Chicken spot. 🍗

Absolutely wonderful. Super tiny dining area with room for 5-ish people, so expect to get takeout. I managed to snag a seat inside and my table service was great--I even got free tap water without asking, just like traditional table service. My chicken and fries were fantastic. The Cajun fries had just enough kick, and the chicken was super crunchy and juicy. I ordered their Memphis BBQ sauce and sweet chili (mild) sauce and both were great! As a St Louisan who loves sweet and smoky bbq, they NAILED IT. Second best BBQ sauce I've ever had, which was totally unexpected. My chicken and fries both came super fresh and were too hot to even eat for a few minutes. They don't skimp on their portions, either; I had to take half of it home, where my friend remarked that he couldn't believe it was still crispy and crunchy after an hour-long ride back to Queens.

Great experience and I'd totally come back.

text:
Even though I don’t sample as many food establishments as I did when I had my first food blog nearly 20 years ago, I find I can still suffer from "food trend fatigue.” After a while, there are only so many things you can do to a burger or do with pizza or fuse one type of cuisine with another before it all becomes rather routine. The “special” dishes that supposedly make a place “unique” are suddenly rather similar to others, and after a while, even the popular, “new” dishes become old hat.
But I will continue to research — and still enjoy, often — what is out there in the culinary cornucopia of options to wind up eventually presently surprised again.

That just happened to be the case today as, on the recommendation of a trusted, fellow epicurean traveler, I tried out a small, new-ish spot up by me here on the Upper East Side of Manhattan called Chicken Insider, which specializes in Korean fried chicken and likewise features a variety of flavors and preparation of the globally ubiquitous fried yardbird.

The innocuous location and way humble build-out of the diminutive spot belies the treasure of crispy fried chicken I enjoyed today. I spoiled myself with an almost intoxicatingly Seoul chicken sandwich showcasing a boneless slab of juicy chicken incased in a crumbly, crispy exterior, “crowned” with robustly spicy sweet “Korean” sauce, then I followed that with the *spicy* Korean sweet chili sauce wings, boasting the same crispy skinned, juicy chicken, generously dressed in an even more satisfyingly tingly sauce.

(It’s almost two hours later since the last wing I ate — though I did bring the last 6 wings home! — and my is still tasting and feeling the bright yet rich heat of that sauce.)

When word spread nearly 10 years ago that the chain Chick-Fil-A was going to open their first locations in New York City, an large number of other chicken-centric spots were soon newly opened or adapted their standard menus to include their versions of “signature” chicken sandwiches. Around the same time new sites for popular Asian fried chicken places started opening up here in Gotham, and more Southern spots opened up promoting their fried chicken as their principal draw. There was quite the hullaballoo when all those places first opened, as they were the shiny new (some hardly new) ideas of that time.

Present day, though, they’re regardeed more in faint memorables (of varying fondness) or mere afterthoughts.
Chicken Insider reminds me of the thrill of (re)discovering the appeal a fried chicken all over again. In my old thinking I’d more expect to find this place down on the Lower East Side, packed and with lines snaking outside from it for hours a day. I appreciate its very convenient geographical proximity, and as well the excitement I now enjoy looking very much forward to revisiting and trying the many other attractive crispy fried chicken dishes on their menu.

title: Blue Ribbon Fried Chicken
text:
Experience here was decent but a few misses that couldn't be ignored but I'll get to that gradually. Coming up here, I could easily smell the chicken being prepared from this establishment and it had me eager to enter the establishment. The moment I came in I was greeted by the woman behind the ordering section so service is definitely a high mark for she was very accommodating with me setting up my order.

Wait time wasn't overly long, I'd say about 7 minutes it took for my food to reach the table. I ordered the Tender Supreme Combo which came with fries, Cole slaw and a drink and a chicken Smashburger. I went with the chicken burger first and I know these can be an acquired taste but I can safely say I truly acquired how good that burger was. Compliments to the chef. Now onto the combo. The shoestring fries they had, not bad but I've certainly had better and they put a lot of them on my plate, I didn't care much to finish it all. I didn't touch the cole slaw because I've never been a fan of it so that leaves the tenders which were sublime! Just incredible. The sides here maybe average but the chicken is definitely solid, tender and juicy with the right amount of breading, wish I could say the same for the Chipotle Honey dip I chose with it. It wasn't terrible but jt didn't mesh well with the tenders, I prolly should've went with ranch. They also have a selection of their own kinds of fountain drinks. I tried out the creme sods and it was also very good. I've always been a fan of original drinks as opposed to the regular stuff that they easily could've had so the fact they went this extra mile for their drinks is great.

As for the place in general, it's pretty big. Not enormous but plenty enough of seating and it wasn't too crowded so I was able to eat in with comfort.

title: Blue Ribbon Fried Chicken
text:
Blue Ribbon Fried Chicken in NYC is a must-visit for anyone who loves perfectly crispy, juicy fried chicken. Located in the East Village, this casual eatery serves up comfort food with a creative twist. The chicken is the star of the show—well-seasoned, golden-brown, and consistently delicious whether you choose bone-in pieces or tenders.

Their sandwich menu is just as impressive. The Classic Sandwich offers a straightforward but satisfying combo of crispy chicken, pickles, and mayo on a potato bun. For something bolder, the Firebird brings heat with pickled peppers and chipotle mayo, while the Blue Ribbon Sandwich adds their signature sauce and fresh veggies for extra flavor. They also feature monthly specials like the Chicken Madness, loaded with BBQ pulled chicken, bacon, and pepper jack cheese.

Sides include crispy fries, creamy coleslaw, and a standout smoked mac and cheese. If you’re in the mood for dessert, their milkshakes are rich and satisfying.

Whether you're grabbing a quick bite or settling in for a hearty meal, Blue Ribbon Fried Chicken delivers comfort food done right. Great flavors, generous portions, and a laid-back vibe make it a reliable go-to in the neighborhood.

text:
Wow, has this place gone down hill. Haven't visited since the pandemic started and first thing I notice are all these changes that the cashier(older woman) said were for the purpose of Covid safety.

Turns out there's another less obvious reason.

First off, I should of realized there were going to be issues when the cashier couldn't even spell my very common first name..I stopped correcting her after 3 tries but figured that I'd be able to make out my name should it be called. She also mentioned having been in a daze recently due to a birthday celebration..after what I eventually experienced, all I could say is no kidding..I should of realized that this was an early tip off to a very sloppily run outfit.

After I very clearly placed my order I then joined a line of people waiting an inordinate amount of time to pick up their food. During this wait time, I notice the very same cashier going over to the preparation area and referencing the order fill monitor above their station instructing/lecturing them on what clearly were issues in the prep part that was causing the backup.

Net net, I finally hear my ticket # and first thing I notice is that they got my order wrong. Out of the 5 options that I specifically requested(2 White meat breasts for example), 4 of them were incorrect. So, I clearly got the wrong order or the counter person inputted it incorrectly..dazed and confused?

Finally, and in support of my earlier comment on why this store is set up like a bio-hazard ward with plexiglass barriers preventing interaction with employees because of "Covid" reasons, it became frustratingly apparent to me that I was not able to communicate the mistaken order I received to even the closest counter person who was 1' away from me on the other side of the barrier.

Additionally, it was obvious to me that this person didn't give a damn about my issue and they could pretend that the barrier between us prevented resolving it. Also, I might note I tried to get the senior cashier's attention about the mistaken order and she, like the counter person, just stared at me like they couldn't understand what I was saying. After 10min of trying to resolve the mistaken order, I finally gave up and went about eating it.

Yes, the chicken was good but seeing all the delivery orders being picked up I can only imagine how many people were going through the same frustration after receiving incorrect deliveries.

At least I was right there in the store and thought I could resolve my issue..or you'd think so.

But alas, due to a combo of mishaps and weaknesses in the process(prep & counter people don't speak English very well & supposed Covid related barriers making direct communication almost impossible..yeah, Covi'd's the reason..yeah right!) I had no luck at all.

Anyway, I'm not going to risk this frustration happening again, especially at a ridiculously inflated cost of $25 for a rather simple order for one; so will not be returning to this restaurant...

Best of luck to anyone who's willing to pay such high prices at a restaurant that's so poorly run..but then again, people might not care that they're paying top dollar and not getting what they ordered..

I'm clearly not okay with that........

title: Blue Ribbon Fried Chicken
text:
So, I’ve been coming here for quite some time and don’t have anything negative to say. Great chicken with a great variety of choices. Some can say the fries are, somewhat, you can call “sexy fries”. Skinny and crispy with some added saltiness.

I always consume their chicken sandwiches and their chicken dogs. I am a huge hotdog lover so I’m glad they have that as a choice. The flavoring is top notch. Not too much but also not too little (I hate it when not enough sauce is provided). You need that sauce.

It’s a perfect lunch spot; a quick grab and go. In all my experiences, probably talking about 20+, I’ve had one questionable experience with one chicken sandwich that the chicken seemed “old”, as in taste wise. Could’ve been an off day so I let it slide.

One thing I would suggest, please add a reward program. Otherwise, definitely a go to spot for my daily lunches.

title: Blue Ribbon Fried Chicken
text:
Exterior wise I'm unsure why there is only one usable entrance when the building has two access points on different streets. The place itself is decorated nicely. The menu is easy to read and understand for a first time visitor. Staff were nice and pleasant to have a transaction with.

Buffalo bites were coated nicely, I wish there was a bit more crunch and heat to them. I'd come back and get the regular bites with a hot sauce on the side. The chicken itself had a great taste and was juicy. The quality of their poultry is excellent. I believe this is where the higher price may come from.

Sweet potato fries were just as you'd expect them to be if you made them from scratch at home, that's a huge plus.

Vanilla milk shake was what you would expect it to taste like. There was nothing special about it.

I'll return to try their chicken sandwiches and other items, one major reason for 4 stars instead of 5 is pricing. For the price I paid, you could go to KFC or Popeyes which is near by and feed an entire family with fried chicken and sides. Is it fair to compare it to a big fast food chain? Not entirely, but when you think of bringing multiple people with you, you start to get conscious of the bill.

title: Greedy Pot
text:
I ordered curried goat, yams, collard greens, and mac and cheese. After waiting 40 minutes, I received potato salad instead of yams, with no call or notice about the substitution.

Unfortunately, the entire meal was disappointing:

The curried goat was overly salty, mostly sharp bones, and lacked freshness.

The potato salad was watery, and the greens were soggy.

The food did not reflect the quality I expect from your restaurant, especially for a Sunday dinner.

I wish someone had contacted me about the missing yams so I could have made a substitution. This lack of communication and quality makes me hesitant to order again.

I hope you take this feedback seriously and consider how to improve both your food preparation and customer service. I’m not seeking a refund—I’m seeking accountability and respect for your patrons.

Let me start off - I love Popeyes. I will take Popeyes fried chicken over almost any other with some standout exceptions, including Charles’ and Melba’s in NYC and McHardy’s in New Orleans.

So this is more of a specific review of the relatively newly released wings. I got a spicy hot six piece. As I was eating them, I could see how it might be hard to stop. It’s kind of an overwhelming supercharged spicy, salty, sweet combination that leaves you feeling that anything else you eat for the rest of your life will taste bland and devoid of flavor.

But when you actually think of flavor, you really there is t much beyond the high salt, high sugar, high heat. The chicken itself has no flavor. The wings are greasy (no surprise) and the breading is probably 60 percent of the mass of the wings in front of you. I’m not sure if the wings are coated in some sort of spice blend, but the external pieces tasted frilly, almost like someone had dumped sand on the wings before serving.

My final takeaway is that these wings taste like the wonderful chicken sandwich, except as if, that sandwich had no roll and no actual chicken. All you are getting is overly spiced breading.

At almost 200 calories PER WING, I’ll take a pass.

I went in at the behest of a friend who wanted junk food, since she doesn't cook. T-Mobile's reward this week was with Popeye's so I downloaded the "supposed" (BOGO gift) reward. I was told by the T-Mobile instruction to download the App, which I did right B4 I entered the store.
Thankfully, I was nearly alone in the store because I asked for help after I showed the cashier the T-Mobile reward.  Another worker said, yes other customers have come in with that reward and that I have to order online and redeem the reward, but make sure its pointed to their store. I did all that. I placed my order, and before I paid for it showed the woman my phone screen and asked if my redemption would come through with my order. She said, "Yes as long as you have chosen our store" and then have me their address.
Well! That didn't happened. I ended up paying for the whole thing. Then the two women I'd asked along each step I took said, "It should" have worked did you point it to this store? Maybe you pointed it to another store." I said, 'No I asked for your help at each step. There was no asking for the reward code, or a redemption process on the order anywhere. They again said it should have worked. Then a male,  possibly a manager, came out and after I told him the events, he tried to tell me I probably used it in another store. I told him I do NOT eat Popeye's and no I pointed it this store, here, today. He then said, he couldn't help me, and probably it was when I went into another store.
I have food allergies, other than going in for a friend, I'd never and have not step foot into a Popeye's since 2014.
I will not  attempt to go again, to redeem anything. They were not helpful.

My friend enjoyed her "junk food", though thankfully. Me, I was just stressed.

title: Popeyes Louisiana Kitchen
text:
Well, all good things have to come to an end. Besides getting old chicken the last 3 times I have been in the store, popeyes has discontinued items that I specifically went to the store for.

They introduced new items like their flounder sandwich, which *could* be good, but a cross section of the fish shows the problem immediately - too much breading. If the top and the bottom breading are each as thick as the fish, that means 2/3 of the main part of the sandwich is made of breading. Add the bun to that, and you have a big bread/carb blob with a small piece of fish tucked inside. The fish would be large enough for the sandwich if the breading was half as thick. If you can't taste the fish, the sandwich is pretty useless. The small amount of tartar sauce was absorbed by the breading, and almost wasn't noticeable. The pickles are as thick as the fish - again, the ratio is wrong. No options for lettuce, tomato, or cheese either. If they offered lettuce, tomato, and cheese on the chicken sandwich, the additions wouldn't be a problem to add to the flounder sandwich. Why is this flounder sandwich on the menu? Oh, of course - to keep lenten fasting from taking people away from Popeyes on Fridays. If the shrimp options were any good, that would have sufficed, but *no one* eats Popeyes shrimp. That is the equivalence of getting a ribeye steak at a deli.

I should have seen the writing on the wall that the jalapeno poppers were on the way out. The jalapeno poppers' signature "pepper jelly" was discontinued 6 months ago, and oddly enough, the employees were instructed to act as if there was never such a thing as this pepper jelly, even though I had purchased the jalapeno poppers with the pepper jelly from that particular store multiple times. Bizarre. Well, they don't need the pepper jelly now, because the jalapeno poppers have been discontinued also.

The real head scratcher is Popeyes discontinuing their cajun rice (dirty rice.) I've been able to get cajun rice from Popeyes since they started in Louisiana in 1972. I'm not exactly sure what they are thinking with discontinuing the cajun rice. The item is a staple that sets them aside from other restaurants. It is quintessential to coastal Louisiana cuisine, and is downright cheap to make in large quantities. I'm pretty stunned about this development. Discontinuing cajun rice is a deal breaker for me about Popeyes.

I have been tolerating getting at least 1 or 2 pieces of dry, old chicken in an order of 5 or more pieces, because I like the sides and cannot get things like the cajun rice at other places. Without the cajun rice, Popeyes is just old, dry chicken. Not a fan anymore, and won't be back. Give it a little time. Once people see their favorites gone from the menu, they won't tolerate the "come and go" quality of the chicken at Popeyes anymore either. Unless the decision to get rid of cajun rice on the menu is reversed in a timely manner, people in NYC have a long memory. Once people have concluded that their favorite menu items aren't coming back, they will write off the store completely, as if it doesn't exist. Then the customer loss will be permanent.

So sad to see Popeyes on the way out in NYC, after they just got here a couple of years ago.

I used to be a loyal customer at this Crown Fried Chicken location, visiting about once a week for years. The food used to be fresh, hot, and consistently good—something I genuinely looked forward to. Unfortunately, that has not been the case recently.

Over the past few weeks, I’ve noticed a serious decline in the quality of their food. The freshness, flavor, and overall preparation just aren’t what they used to be. Most concerning of all, a few days ago I purchased some chicken and ended up with a terrible stomachache after eating it. The pain was so intense that I couldn’t sleep that night. This was a very disappointing and alarming experience, especially coming from a place I used to trust.

I’m not sure what has changed—whether it’s the ingredients, the cooking process, or management—but something is definitely going downhill here. I hope the owners or staff take this feedback seriously and bring the quality back to the standard it once was. Until then, I’ll be staying away.

title: Charles Pan-Fried Chicken
text:
Charles Pan-Fried Chicken on the Upper West Side instantly transported me back to the soul food spots I loved in Atlanta. The fried chicken was perfectly seasoned and crispy, with that signature pan-fried crunch that’s hard to find anywhere outside the South.

The sides were absolutely spot-on — creamy mac n cheese, sweet candied yams, and perfectly cooked collard greens that tasted like they came straight from someone’s Sunday dinner table. The sweet tea was solid — not quite Georgia sweet, but close enough to pair well with the meal.

What really stood out was the hospitality. The service was out of this world — warm, welcoming, and genuinely kind. You can tell it’s family-operated, and it feels like they’ve invited you into their home for a meal.

If you’re craving real-deal soul food in New York, this is it. Charles’ place is a gem, and I’ll definitely be back.

It's a spring 2025 girl's trip, and we had to come back to a favorite, Charles Pan Fried Chicken! I LOVE the vibe of this place. Manager Elaine greeted us, along with hey staff, BIG smiles, and a WELCOME TO CHARLES PAN FRIED CHICKEN! 3 piece chicken, 2 BIG sides 18.95! The food is consistently good! --------------------
The Girls and I visited NYC this week and had the pleasure of grabbing some of the BEST comfort food EVER! I had been following Charles Pan Fried Chicken on IG, and I wanted to make sure we were able to enjoy this experience!

We had been shopping and dropped our bags off on our room and hopped on the Subway at 42nd St and took it out to Central Park West and 72nd. We followed 72nd about 3 blocks and went in!

It's a VERY small location (1 of 4; Flagship in Harlem; Another one at 125th; this one on 72nd and another on the upper East side).  There were 3 chairs at a counter and 4 of us. So, 3 of us sat in the chairs and 1 in the window pane opening.  We all ordered the same thing (3 piece chicken, 2 sides, corn bread, and a drink); this totaled about $22, including tax. I had black-eyed peas and collards  as my sides; two of my friends had okra/white rice and green beans, and the other had mac and cheese and collards.

The food was delicious and the portions generous! I took it down a star, as I really wish the were a couple more chairs/tables. We ate and had plenty left over to snack on as we packed to return home!

I highly recommend if you are in the city!

The instagram influencers reminded me this place was on my bucket list of restaurants to try. Its walking distance from Lincoln Center and will be my go to place when Im in the  neighborhood.

Ordered:
Mac and cheese- personal preference wish the cheese on top was broiled for that nice crunch on top. You can see the pepper specks as in its nicely seasoned.

Yam- I usually dont like yams because a lot of people make it overly sweet and watery. This yam was not too sweet and soft

Cornbread- soft and pillowy like

Fried Chicken (dark meat)- nice and juicy, crispy and the meat itself taste like it was brined or pre seasoned. Highly recommend you try it!

Con: theres only 3 seats and this place is take out.

Customer Service- Everyone was super nice and friendly!

They have a nice selection of other menu items like okra, black eye peas and dessert. I will be back to try them!

To management:
Please come to Dekalb market or somewhere in Brooklyn thanks!

title: Passaic Fried Chicken
text:
Mostly because I've been coming here since my teenage years when I lived in Passaic, (over 20 years now) and now that I moved out of the area, I can't lie, and I'm not the only one that feels that way, but you need a 'fix' of what we call some "ghetto chicken". Formerly Monroe chicken, Passaic was filled with these such as Dixie's, on Passaic Street, and American Fried Chicken at the corner of Myrtle and Monroe. Since then, all of them have closed. This one remains open though. Ever since Mayor Sammy Rivera imposed an ordinance that would change the hours and rules for staying open without a certain number of seats for patrons, it hasn't been the same with the late night hours, but it's not the establishments fault. There has been one that opened on Passaic Street near the Aspen projects, I believe it is Tiny's ? or something like that, but it is within the past 10 years, and I can't comment on it because I've never been there. But something that is undoubted is this place's longevity, and they are very patient and a chill staff, considering the Dynamics of the many different customers that arrive. Let's face it, we know the area, some people come in twisted from Friday or Saturday night outings, or some of them may just be the same way on a Tuesday morning... But loud, boisterous, demanding and sometimes impatient, or rude as heck, so you got to admit as customers here, these guys deal with the lot of stuff. It's no wonder they got that thick plastic glass, if not only for the safety reasons but just because some people's breath. Lol.
But I like the staff, the older guys that of course we have turned Habibi Grandma more likely out of ignorance, but even the gentleman that we turn that allowed it and welcome for the name. I like the new younger dude. Alot actually ;-)
If you think about that, these people have been in our communities for decades now and it has allowed me to understand that they are just like all of us, far before the ignorance of the haters and people like Trump supporters, who think all middle easterns are in a stigma. These people are hard-working people that serve us halal food for years. They're in their sweating just as much as us. I could say though I do know they make enough money to put air condition in the place. That's why they'll get four stars instead of 5. If people loiter or they are there too long and abusing the air condition and they are not customers, you simply need to ask them to leave. Otherwise there is seats for people that are customers to eat, but you cannot eat there in the summer. Too hot
I also like the idea that this place has regular, plain buffalo wings. Not just spicy, hot wings. All of the ones in Bloomfield and Belleville and Newark near me only have spicy hot wings and I can't tolerate that anymore at my age and health, so I always have to order something else when I do go to these places.
They are good though. I recommend them. and there's so many memories I have here that even though I said four because of the air condition, I'll still get five stars.
